page: Amazon Web Services r8i.24xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs spanning 48 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz. The compute subsystem is equipped with a large 480 MB L3 cache and supports specialized instruction extensions including AVX-512, AMX-TILE, AMX-INT8, and cryptographic acceleration. System memory totals 768.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM clocked at 7 GHz, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for memory-demanding processing.

In benchmark evaluations, the r8i.24xlarge demonstrates exceptional throughput in concurrent and memory-bound operations. Large-block read memory bandwidth achieves 384.5 GB/sec, placing it in the top tier of evaluated systems, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 657.04 GB/sec. The instance delivers high throughput in data-handling scenarios, recording 171.48 million Redis SET operations per second and a PassMark database operations metric of 33,046.14. It also records competitive multi-threaded performance in PassMark CPU tests (106,946.29) and LLM prompt processing workloads via hardware matrix acceleration.

The instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 40 Gbps but includes no local NVMe storage, requiring network-attached storage architectures for persistent data needs. Additionally, it lacks dedicated hardware GPUs, relying solely on CPU-level AMX vector operations for inference workloads. Given its balanced 1:8 vCPU-to-memory density, high memory bandwidth, and substantial core allocation, the r8i.24xlarge is engineered for in-memory databases, large Redis clusters, enterprise ERP deployments, big data caching, and distributed multi-threaded analytics.
description: Amazon Web Services r8i.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance engineered for data-intensive processing within the AWS Nitro framework. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz, it features 96 dedicated vCPUs (48 physical cores) alongside 480 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX-512 and AMX instructions. It incorporates 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, offering a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory allocation. Benchmark results highlight top-tier performance across multi-threaded execution, with large-block memory read bandwidth reaching 384.5 GB/sec, 171.48 million Redis SET operations per second, and a PassMark CPU score of 106,946.29. The server provides 40 Gbps baseline networking but provides no local storage and no dedicated GPUs, relying on remote volumes. This configuration provides high resource density and operational efficiency for in-memory data grids, large-scale caching, relational databases, and enterprise data analytics.
